summary.headline: Best UK opportunity today: MTD implementation still leads, with e-invoicing and cash-collection automation the strongest commercial second bet.
summary.best_opportunity: Making Tax Digital onboarding, cleanup and quarterly-support automation for sole traders, landlords and small accountancy firms
summary.why_now: Live GOV.UK guidance updated in March 2026 says MTD for Income Tax starts from 6 April 2026 for qualifying income above £50,000, expands to £30,000 from 6 April 2027 and £20,000 from 6 April 2028. That creates immediate setup demand now plus recurring quarterly workflow support after onboarding.

top_opportunities.name: Making Tax Digital onboarding and quarterly-support automation
top_opportunities.description: Sell a fixed-scope implementation package that checks MTD eligibility, cleans records, connects bookkeeping software, sets reminder workflows and supports quarterly updates for sole traders, landlords and small firms.
top_opportunities.why_now: Evidence is strong. GOV.UK says qualifying income above £50,000 for the 2024 to 2025 tax year must use MTD from 6 April 2026, then £30,000 from 6 April 2027 and £20,000 from 6 April 2028. This is live compliance demand with a direct service wedge.
top_opportunities.buyer: Sole traders, landlords, independent bookkeepers and small accountancy practices
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: High - setup fee plus monthly or quarterly support
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Excellent for a solo engineer because the first sale is migration, workflow setup and admin reduction rather than building a full accounting platform.
risks: Accounting software vendors already own the ledger, so the wedge must be onboarding, cleanup and reporting admin
Avoid regulated tax advice and position the offer as implementation and workflow support
top_opportunities.verdict: Best overall because the trigger is current, the offer can be sold immediately as a service, and recurring support is built in.

top_opportunities.name: E-invoicing rollout and receivables automation for SMEs
top_opportunities.description: Offer a productized service or lightweight SaaS that standardises invoice creation, automates reminders, tracks promises to pay and gives owners a simple overdue-cash dashboard.
top_opportunities.why_now: Evidence is strong. A March 2026 GOV.UK study says 80% of SMEs still mainly send PDF or email invoices, so adoption headroom is real. The November 2025 government consultation response says e-invoicing can cut invoicing costs by 60% to 80%, reduce late payments by 20% and save small firms about £11,300 annually. A May 2026 GOV.UK announcement also says late payments cost the UK economy £11 billion every year.
top_opportunities.buyer: Micro businesses, agencies, consultancies, trades firms and other B2B service SMEs
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: High - monthly subscription or managed receivables retainer
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Very strong for a solo engineer because the work is mainly integrations, workflow rules, reminder logic and reporting.
risks: Some buyers will assume their accounting package already solves this unless the pitch is framed around debtor days and collected cash
Messy source data across Xero, QuickBooks and spreadsheet-led workflows can slow onboarding
top_opportunities.verdict: Probably the best non-compliance opportunity because the pain is immediate cashflow and the ROI is easy to demonstrate fast.

top_opportunities.name: Tender monitoring and bid-drafting assistant for SME suppliers
top_opportunities.description: Create a focused tool or managed service that monitors relevant tenders, scores fit, drafts first-pass answers and stores reusable case-study, pricing and compliance evidence.
top_opportunities.why_now: Evidence is good. Procurement Act guidance updated in 2026 says contracting authorities must have regard to barriers faced by SMEs, and Procurement Policy Note 001 says the reforms are intended to make it easier for small businesses to access public sector supply chains with greater visibility of upcoming opportunities. That creates room for a narrow monitoring and drafting layer.
top_opportunities.buyer: Small consultancies, digital agencies, specialist service firms and compliance-heavy B2B suppliers
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Medium to high - retainer, seat fee or managed bid support
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Good for an engineer who can combine data collection, document generation and workflow tooling into one narrow offer.
risks: Tender demand is episodic, so revenue can be lumpier than tax or payment services
Bid-writing agencies already exist, so the offer needs automation leverage or a tight niche
top_opportunities.verdict: A credible niche B2B play if aimed at one supplier category instead of the whole procurement market.

top_opportunities.name: Cyber Essentials readiness and evidence-collection automation
top_opportunities.description: Offer a fixed-scope package covering MFA, backups, account hygiene, device checks, phishing guidance and evidence collection for small organisations that need a stronger baseline or want to bid for contracts.
top_opportunities.why_now: Evidence is solid. GOV.UK updated its Cyber Essentials overview in March 2026 and says over 215,000 certificates have been awarded, including 49,248 in the past 12 months. It also says an up-to-date certificate enables a business to bid for government contracts where financial or personal data is involved. That supports a checklist-driven, productized service.
top_opportunities.buyer: Small professional firms, charities, clinics, agencies and B2B service SMEs
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Medium to high - monitoring, policy reviews and periodic checks
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Good if you prefer structured technical delivery and keep the service standardized.
risks: Trust matters in security work, so some buyers will prefer established specialists
If the service becomes too bespoke, part-time solo delivery gets much harder
top_opportunities.verdict: Viable as a standardized technical service, especially where certification unlocks contracts or supply-chain access.

top_opportunities.name: AI lead-response and admin automation for local service firms
top_opportunities.description: Productize missed-call text-back, instant web-form replies, quote follow-up, booking handoff and a basic pipeline dashboard for firms that lose work through slow response times.
top_opportunities.why_now: Evidence is more directional than the top four. The AI Opportunities Action Plan still frames AI as a growth and productivity priority for the UK, which helps sales conversations, but that is not the same as a hard buying trigger. This opportunity is strongest when sold as recovered leads and fewer admin hours, not as generic AI consulting.
top_opportunities.buyer: Plumbers, electricians, HVAC firms, clinics, salons, cleaning firms and other local service operators
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Strong for a solo engineer because the stack is mostly messaging, CRM glue, forms, scheduling and reporting.
risks: Competition is visible, so a narrow niche and hard ROI framing are essential
Evidence for urgency is weaker than compliance or payment pain, so proof with before-and-after metrics matters
top_opportunities.verdict: Still attractive, but only if packaged as a narrow, ROI-led automation service rather than a broad AI agency offer.

best_pick.name: Making Tax Digital onboarding and quarterly-support automation
best_pick.why_it_wins: It has the clearest live trigger, fits a solo engineer on a low budget, can be sold as a service before any software build-out, and naturally converts into recurring quarterly support or bookkeeping-adjacent admin retainers.
validation_plan: Pick one wedge first: landlords with simple property records or small accountancy firms that need extra MTD onboarding capacity.
Build a tiny demo showing record capture, reminder workflows and a client-status dashboard on top of off-the-shelf bookkeeping software.
Publish a fixed-price MTD readiness package with clear scope, turnaround time and a monthly or quarterly support option.
Contact 30 to 50 local accountants, bookkeepers and landlord-focused businesses before building anything beyond dashboards and automation glue.
best_pick.first_offer: MTD readiness setup for sole traders and landlords: records cleanup, software connection, reminder workflows and first-quarter support. Charge roughly £299 to £799 setup plus £39 to £149 per month depending on complexity.
best_pick.mvp: A thin internal tool plus off-the-shelf bookkeeping software, document capture, reminder automation and a simple dashboard for onboarding status and quarterly check-ins.
customer_types: Sole traders above the current MTD threshold
best_pick.do_today: Create a one-page MTD readiness offer, build a dashboard mock-up and start direct outreach to local accountants and landlord-facing businesses today.
